title: Kernel lifecycle and lazy-KV binding experiments
content:
Purpose:
This note collects informal experiments and design sketches for a lightweight kernel lifecycle that lazily binds paged KV into FlashAttention/fused-op kernels. Goal: reduce tail latency for long-context requests while avoiding wasted memory transfer and expensive full-KV materialization. This is exploratory — contains rough numbers, TODOs, and heuristics to test in CI harness.

Background and motivation:
- FlashAttention-style fused attention kernels are extremely efficient for dense contiguous attention, but when KV is paged (on-GPU mix of resident + on-demand), the common pattern is either: (a) materialize a contiguous KV tile per request (fast kernels, high transfer), or (b) run many small kernels per-page (low transfer, high kernel overhead).
- We want a middle ground: a kernel lifecycle that can accept an abstract KV view, trigger minimal DMA for missing pages, and either block-wait for pages or return partial results with incremental continuation. This must cooperate with scheduler policies (latency SLO vs cost), batching, and occupancy constraints.

Concept: lazy-KV binding & kernel lifecycle
1) Kernel entry protocol (lightweight):
   - kernel receives a KV handle (opaque page map + resident bitmap) and target seq-lens for query/key/value windows.
   - If resident bitmap shows >X% locality (heuristic), launch a fused FlashAttention kernel that expects contiguous staging regions.
   - Otherwise, fall back to paging-aware microkernels that operate per-page with async-completion hooks.
2) Lazy binding:
   - Kernel does not assume pages already resident. At a well-defined prefetch point it calls a device-side prefetch stub that enqueues page requests into a shared per-stream prefetch queue (ring).
   - Prefetch queue processed by a low-latency prefetch controller thread (CPU or dedicated stream), which issues cudaMemcpyAsync for missing pages into pre-allocated staging slabs.
3) Continuation semantics:
   - Kernel registers a lightweight continuation (4-8 byte cookie) into a per-request continuation list. When prefetch completes the kernel resumes via a short resume kernel (<< full fused kernel).
   - Two resume modes: (a) partial-resume — patch-in a small region and continue; (b) full-resume — re-run the heavy fused kernel if fragmentation exceeded threshold.
4) Fallback policy:
   - If request critical (SLO tight) and prefetch latency > deadline, fallback to smaller-window microkernel with approximate attention (e.g., block-sparse) to preserve latency.

Implementation notes / micro-optimizations tried:
- Prefetch batching: group page requests across concurrent requests in same stream by aligning to 128KB slabs. Reduced per-request DMA ops by ~32% in early tests.
- Staging buffer pooling: pre-allocate slab pools per-GPU sized for 4x average resident working set; reuse to avoid cudaMalloc/free cost.
- Warp-level coalescing: when reading KV from staging slabs, use warp-cooperative reads into shared memory in 128B chunks to preserve memory coalescing for non-contiguous pages.
- Atomic rendezvous counter: used an 8-byte atomic per-request to count page completions; avoid expensive global synchronization. Works well when page counts are small (<64).
- Kernel size heuristics: empirically found break-even for running fused kernel vs page-microkernel around 55–65% contiguous resident fraction (depends on model size and block size). Tunable via runtime flag.

Experiment matrix (selected runs) — single-A100, 1-infer worker, synthetic traces:
- Baseline contiguous materialize-then-fused: median P50=12.4ms, P95=28.6ms, cost: high (GPU memcpy dominated).
- Microkernel-per-page (no fusion): P50=9.1ms, P95=42.3ms, cost: lower memory transfers but high kernel overhead -> bad P95.
- Lazy-binding fuse+resume (heuristic threshold 60%): P50=10.2ms, P95=22.1ms. Best trade-off for mixed locality traces.
- Aggressive prefetch (overfetch 2x): P50=11.0ms, P95=18.9ms but memory usage + bandwidth spike up 1.7x.
Notes: numbers are noisy; need multi-GPU and mixed-batch tests.

Memory layout and page format suggestions:
- Page size: 64KB slab that stores kv vectors interleaved per head to allow contiguous head-major access inside attention kernel. This reduces shuffles inside kernel for multi-head layouts.
- Page headers: store sequence-start, valid-mask, LRU-timestamp (u64), compressed-quant-flag. Keep header small (32 bytes) and aligned to 64B to avoid cache thrashing.
- Staging alignment: 128B alignment recommended to leverage best L2 coalescing patterns on Ampere/Hopper.

Scheduling interactions and tradeoffs:
- Batch-aware prefetching: when autoscaler/coalescer merges small requests into a microbatch, prefetch controller can piggyback pages for all requests -> significant wins for PLG spikes. Requires serialized prefetch plan computation (cheap heuristic).
- Priority preemption: mark SLO-critical requests so their prefetch ops get higher priority on the prefetch queue. Implementation via separate priority rings reduces head-of-line blocking.
- Kernel packing: avoid launching giant fused kernels if the batch has heterogeneous sequence lengths — split by length bands and pick kernel variant. We implemented 3 variants: short/medium/long with different shared-memory tilings.

Quantization and fused-op implications:
- Low-bit quantized KV (4/8-bit) reduces DMA cost but complicates fused kernels because quant->fp32 unpacking cost is per-token. Two strategies: (a) decompress into staging slabs before fuse (adds local copy cost), (b) integrate dequant path into fused kernel (more complex but saves memory copy).
- Our experiments favored integrated dequant for 4-bit when contiguous fraction >75%; otherwise decompress-to-stage then run microkernel.

Open problems and TODOs:
- Continuation inefficiency: currently resume kernel sometimes re-executes expensive setup work. Need a smaller resume kernel that can patch only the missing KV windows into precomputed softmax buffers. TODO: design resume-kernel ABI and test overhead.
- Cross-stream page deduplication: prefetch queue duplicates page requests across streams — we need a global hash table to collapse duplicates with cancellation token. Careful: synchronization cost vs reduced DMA.
- Fault and eviction model: how to handle a page evicted mid-request if LRU collides with active prefetches. Proposed: mark page pinned while continuation cookie exists; eviction deferred until refcount zero.
- Integration with runtime rollout: fallbacks must be configurable per-deployment tier (hosted/dedicated/private). Need config knobs in route config and console visibility for prefetch bandwidth.

Action items and experiments to run:
- [ ] Build small resume-kernel prototype (Evan or Miguel) and measure extra setup overhead vs re-run full fused kernel.
- [ ] Implement cross-stream dedupe in prefetch controller and simulate with synthetic traces.
- [ ] Run multi-GPU batch tests with real request traces from hosted API (anon) to validate P95 improvements and bandwidth spikes.
- [ ] Add telemetry counters for per-request prefetch page counts, resume counts, fallback triggers. Wire into local dev dashboard.

Questions for the next design sync:
- What is acceptable memory overhead (staging pool) for Hosted vs Dedicated customers?
- How do we expose fallback policies in API (auto vs opt-in)?
- Should we prioritize integrated dequant in fused kernels (more engineering cost) or keep as heuristic for now?

References and links:
- PR: serving-runtime#782 — early prefetch-ring impl
- Confluence: paged-KV architecture draft (internal)
- Jira: RT-1452 — prefetch controller backlog

Notes to self:
- Keep experiments reproducible: add full env + seed in benchmark harness.
- Latency numbers above from quick bench; expect 10–20% variance on different GPU generations.

Rough timeline proposal:
- Q1: prototype resume-kernel + staging pool integration, basic telemetry.
- Q2: cross-stream dedupe, priority rings, and exploit batch-level prefetching.
- Q3: integrate dequant path into fused kernel for 4-bit and run validation across hosted cluster.

Appendix: rough pseudocode sketch (conceptual)
(kept simple for now)
- request arrives -> compute locality fraction -> if fraction >= threshold launch fused-with-prefetch-kernel else microkernel-flow.
- fused-with-prefetch-kernel:
  prefetch_list = collect_missing_pages();
  enqueue_prefetch(prefetch_list, continuation_cookie);
  return (park) // kernel exits quickly
- prefetch controller -> on completion, write pages into staging slabs and atomically increment cookie
- resume worker reads cookie, if fully satisfied launches resume-kernel to finish attention compute and write response.

End of note.
